A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bar headed geese have a reduced oxygen demand and increased oxygen delivery during hypoxia, compared with low altitude migrating geese.
high-altitude rearing of bar-headed geese does not appear to be a major factor in their ability to fly at high altitude.
the bar headed geese are well suited for high altitude living and migration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bar-headed geese reared in high altitude exhibit physiological characteristics that may help them cope with the hypoxia they experience during their migratory flight over the Himalayas.
the ability to fly over the Himalayas is not a result of phenotypic plastic responses to high altitude, but rather a result of the species being adapted to high altitudes.
bar headed geese, a species that migrates across some of the most challenging terrain in the world, have evolved a suite of cardiovascular and respiratory adaptations that facilitate this feat.
